long_biography.plain_text:
Stanford computer-science student Lucas Duplan began developing Clinkle before graduation. The payments company attracted an unusually large seed round, largely through convertible debt, while Duplan kept substantial equity and control. Outside financing belonged to the business, not its founder. A possible sale was explored, but no completed acquisition became public. Operations ended in 2016, and there is no disclosed liquidity event for Duplan.

By 2018, Duplan had raised an investment vehicle backed by relatives and outside investors to support enterprise-software companies. He backed an employee-rewards business but was no longer operationally involved there. His latest professional description is simply technology ventures.
